title: Review: Use of amount of substance in relation to masses of pure substances; Yield and atom economy of chemical reactions (chemistry only); Using concentrations of solutions in mol/dm 3 (chemistry only) (HT only); Use of amount of substance in relation to volumes of gases (chemistry only) (HT only); Reactivity of metals

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Atom economy (atom utilisation)
items.clue: A measure of the amount of starting materials that end up as useful products.

items.label: Displacement reaction
items.clue: A reaction in which a more reactive metal takes the place of a less reactive metal in a compound.

items.label: Redox reaction
items.clue: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen together: oxygen lost by one substance is gained by another.

items.label: Side reaction
items.clue: A reaction in which some of the reactants react in ways different to the expected reaction, forming a substance other than the desired product.

questions.stem: Which calculation gives the percentage yield of a product?

options.text: (maximum theoretical mass of product / mass of the product made) x 100
(mass of product actually made / total mass of all reactants) x 100
(Mr of the desired product / sum of Mr of all reactants) x 100
(mass of product actually made / maximum theoretical mass) x 100

questions.explanation: Correct: the specification formula is % Yield = (Mass of product actually made) / (Maximum theoretical mass of product) x 100.

questions.stem: Titanium is extracted by the reaction TiCl4 + 4Na -> Ti + 4NaCl. Mr: TiCl4 = 190, Na = 23, Ti = 48, NaCl = 58.5. What is the percentage atom economy for titanium?
In separate tests, metal A displaces metal B from its sulfate solution, and metal B displaces metal C from its sulfate solution. What can be concluded?

options.text: A is the most reactive of the three and C the least.
C is the most reactive and A the least reactive.
A and B are ordered, but C cannot be placed.
All three are equally reactive as all reacted.

questions.explanation: The two results chain together into one order, A above B above C, which is exactly how an order of reactivity is deduced from results.

questions.stem: 6.0 g of magnesium is burned in air. The maximum theoretical mass of magnesium oxide is 10.0 g. The student collects 8.5 g of magnesium oxide. What is the percentage yield?
Give one reason why it is important for a company to use a reaction with a high atom economy.

options.text: More of the product predicted by the equation is collected each time.
Less of the starting material is wasted, so raw materials cost less.
The reaction runs faster, so more product is made in the same time.
No by-products are made at all, so there is no waste to deal with.

questions.explanation: Correct: more of the starting material ends up as useful product, which matters for sustainable development, because raw materials are limited, and for economic reasons.

questions.stem: The maximum theoretical mass of a product is 60 g. A student separates and dries the product and obtains 54 g of it. What is the percentage yield?
The relative formula mass (Mr) of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃, is 100. What is the mass of one mole of calcium carbonate?

options.text: 1 g

questions.explanation: The mass of one mole in grams is numerically equal to the relative formula mass, so one mole of CaCO₃ has a mass of 100 g.

questions.stem: The equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O can be interpreted in terms of moles. Which reading of it is correct?

options.text: Two grams of H₂ react with one gram of O₂ gas.
H₂ and O₂ react in a 2 : 1 ratio by mass.
Two molecules of H₂ give one molecule of H₂O.
Two moles of H₂ react with one mole of O₂.

questions.explanation: The balancing numbers give the amounts in moles: two moles of hydrogen to one mole of oxygen.

questions.stem: 4.0 g of hydrogen (Mr of H₂ = 2), 32 g of oxygen (Mr of O₂ = 32) and 36 g of water (Mr of H₂O = 18) are measured in a reaction. Which balanced equation fits these masses?

options.text: 4H₂ + 2O₂ → 4H₂O
4H₂ + 32O₂ → 36H₂O
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
H₂ + O₂ → H₂O

questions.explanation: 4.0 ÷ 2 = 2 mol H₂, 32 ÷ 32 = 1 mol O₂ and 36 ÷ 18 = 2 mol H₂O, a ratio of 2 : 1 : 2.

questions.stem: Magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. A student adds 0.10 mol of magnesium to 0.10 mol of hydrochloric acid. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The magnesium is limiting, as it has the smaller mass.
Neither reactant is limiting, as the amounts match.
The magnesium is the limiting reactant in this mixture.
The hydrochloric acid is the limiting reactant.

questions.explanation: 0.10 mol of Mg needs 0.20 mol of HCl, so the acid runs out first and the magnesium is in excess.

questions.stem: Iron is extracted in the blast furnace: Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. Mr: Fe2O3 = 160, Fe = 56. What is the maximum theoretical mass of iron that can be made from 20 g of iron(III) oxide?

options.text: 7 g

questions.explanation: Correct: 20 / 160 = 0.125 mol of Fe2O3, and the 2 in 2Fe gives 0.25 mol of Fe, so the mass is 0.25 x 56 = 14 g.

questions.stem: What amount, in moles, of sodium hydroxide is present in 250 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.200 mol/dm³?

options.text: 50.0 mol
0.8 mol

questions.explanation: amount in moles = concentration × volume in dm³ = 0.200 × 0.250 = 0.0500 mol.
